36/G.goal: Explain contextual inquiry and apply affinity diagrams to convert observed user behavior into usability requirements and design recommendations.
36/G.achieves: This gives the learner a user-centered method for moving from requirement gathering to usability specification during XR system development.

36/O1.goal: Explain how contextual inquiry is organized as a staged observational method, including active and passive modes, the master-apprentice observer stance, and reflection through affinity diagrams.
36/O1.achieves: This lets the learner collect usability evidence from users in real task contexts and prepare that evidence for requirement-gathering work in an XR system development case study.

36/O2.goal: Apply affinity diagrams to group contextual inquiry notes and observations into design recommendations and requirement categories while distinguishing requirements from implementation choices.
36/O2.achieves: This lets the learner convert observed user needs into usable requirement specifications for later design and implementation of an XR system.
